newsitem.title: USA: American HealthChoice sees yr '96 loss.
newsitem.headline: American HealthChoice sees yr '96 loss.

text.p: American HealthChoice Inc said Tuesday it expects to report a "significant loss" for the 12 months ended September 30.

Company President J. Wes Stucki said in a telephone interview that the loss is due to a $1.1 million Medicaid receivable, which is currently the subject of an administrative proceeding, increased corporate overhead and additions being made to its bad debt reserve.

American HealthChoice, which owns and manages a network of primary care medical clinics in Texas, Louisiana and Georgia, said it has decided to delay filing its annual report for the year ended September 30. The report is expected to be filed on or about January 31, it said.
For the 12 months ended September 30, 1995, the company reported net income of $649,167, or $0.20 per share, Stucki said.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk, 212 859-1610))
